newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia ferries 138 boatpeople to mainland.
newsitem.headline: Australia ferries 138 boatpeople to mainland.

text.p: Australia's Immigration Department on Saturday ferried 138 boatpeople from an island off Queensland this week to the mainland.

A customs boat on Friday guided the group to Thursday Island in the Torres Strait between Australia and Papua New Guinea after their trawler was stranded on a sandbank, an Immigration Department spokeswoman told Reuters.
"We don't yet know where they are from or why they are here," she said.

A few hundred illegal immigrants arrive at Australia by boat each year, usually from east Asia but at times from as far away as Romania and Poland. Almost all are detained and eventually returned to their country of origin.
The department spokeswoman said the latest group, all but two of whom were male, would be taken to the Port Hedland detention centre on the northwest coast.
Australia currently had 182 boatpeople in detention, she said.
